rules.name: Retired CTG stats blocklist (regex, JS sources)

value.rationale: retired stat "3,000+ hours" — the canonical number is 4,000+
retired stat "125 Gurus" — the canonical number is 120+
retired stat "50 categories" — the canonical number is 58

rules.name: Vendor neutrality watchlist and peer TSDs
Vendor neutrality operating rule
rules.value: Names on the neutrality-watchlist vendors list are NEVER presented as CTG choices or recommendations; they may appear only inside a constraint statement. Recommend fit, not favorites: no promotional tone toward, and no undisclosed bias for, any named vendor. Competitive framing targets peer-TSD positioning only (Telarus, Avant, Intelisys) and never disparages a vendor CTG stays neutral on. Commission economics are disclosed transparently wherever recommendations or pricing appear; hidden economics is a fail, transparency is the selling point.

rules.name: Person
rules.value: Second person by default. First-person plural for CTG's position. Never first-person singular on any CTG surface.

rules.name: Claim first
rules.value: The claim appears in sentence 1. No preamble, no throat-clearing, no scene-setting before the claim.

rules.name: One primary ask
rules.value: Exactly one primary ask per asset. An asset with zero asks is a defect, not a style choice; two asks is a block.

rules.name: Proof points are human-supplied
rules.value: Exactly one CTG proprietary proof point per article and per convert post, supplied by a human. The agent never generates, rounds, interpolates, or remembers a CTG figure; a missing proof point escalates instead of publishing.

rules.name: No third-party stat openers
rules.value: Zero third-party statistics in the first sentence, title, or H1. Any third-party figure used later carries a supplied source URL or is dropped, never paraphrased.

rules.name: No suppliers, TSDs, or politics
rules.value: Zero named suppliers, zero named competing TSDs, zero political content. Hard block on every surface including titles, alt text, and image prompts.

rules.name: Banned vocabulary blocks
rules.value: Zero banned-vocabulary terms. Hard block with substitution from the substitutions table; a term that survives substitution stops publication.

rules.name: Hashtag limits
rules.value: At most 3 hashtags, end of post only, never inside body text, drawn from the closed pillar-keyed library. A post under 25 words carrying 4 or more hashtags is a hard block.

rules.name: Emoji limits
rules.value: At most 2 emoji per LinkedIn post, zero in articles, never in the first sentence of a commercial or technical post, never as the sole carrier of meaning, none in Governance, Regulation, or Healthcare posts.

rules.name: No math-alphanumeric unicode
rules.value: No math-alphanumeric bold or italic unicode characters anywhere in generated output; they break screen readers. Plain sentence case for opening lines.

rules.name: Tag every asset
rules.value: Every asset names its pillar, funnel bucket, hook style, and CTA type at generation time so performance stays attributable.

rules.name: Unfilled placeholder is a defect
rules.value: If a required bracket, variable, or proof point cannot be filled with a specific true value, the asset does not publish; it drafts and escalates. An unfilled placeholder is a hard block.

rules.name: One metaphor maximum
rules.value: One metaphor per asset, stated once in the headline or lede, then dropped. Never sustain a metaphor across sections; never mix metaphors.

value.transformation: the specific change: migration, consolidation, re-platform

rules.name: Pillar: Healthcare CX (human review, regulatory exposure)
Pillar: Gen Z & Expectations (LinkedIn only, not article-eligible)
Pillar: BPO & Outsourcing (reframe: never open on a cost or outsourcing statistic; lead with CTG's boundary position)
Pillar: Regulation & Industry (reframe: dated-obligation format only, never a news recap; human review; not article-eligible)
Pillar: Governance & Neutrality (experimental, touches the commercial model, human review)
Pillar: Vertical Expansion, Financial Services and Retail (experimental, human review on first-in-vertical)
Pillar: CX General (review queue; never auto-assigned, resolving here means the asset drafts for human review)

value.note: canonical mix per Playbook §3/§6.2; the 70/20/10 figure in older CTG docs is superseded. Service-ask share target at least 0.15.

rules.name: Prohibited opener patterns
value: third_party_statistic: any external statistic as the opener, title, or H1
pull_quote: a quote with no preceding claim of CTG's own
third_party_company_news: a named third party's announcement or news recap
bare_announcement_no_idea: an announcement carrying no idea, the it's-live shape
pronoun_with_no_referent: an opener whose pronoun points at nothing shown
tease_and_defer: a deferral phrase as the payload with no independent claim in sentence 1
rules.source: AUTOMATION_CONFIG.json prohibited_hooks; BRAND_VOICE.md §11 prohibited openers; QUALITY_AND_SAFETY_RULES.md HB-59

value.structure: Lede (claim, two-beat payoff, reader stake, promise); H2 named framework as an extractable definition block; H2 the translation, one metaphor; 3-4 H2 criteria/steps/failure-mode sections, one table or one list each; H2 what it looks like gone wrong, anonymised pattern; H2 FAQ, 5 questions answered standalone in 40-70 words, FAQPage schema; H2 conclusion with single CTA and proof point. Nurture. Human review on first publication. Companions LB-02 then LB-04.

Flat contrarian claim, no hedging; the autopsy as a 3-stage anonymised pattern (what was bought, what broke, what it cost operationally); the negation, not because of the obvious cause; the systemic cause in one sentence plus 3 concrete failure modes as a list; the practitioner credential line; conclusion and single CTA. Title T2 or T3. Reach funnel.

The translation stated as sentence 1; why the CX term hides the engineering reality; the pathology the engineering term brings, 3 concrete consequences; what to measure instead as a short table; one vendor question the reader can use verbatim; conclusion linking up to the pillar. Title T1. Reach funnel. Requires a definition block.

The decision framed as the wrong question the reader is asking; the right question in one sentence; decision table, 4-6 criteria by 2-3 options, criteria owned by CTG; the variable that actually decides it, named; the cost line nobody invoiced, 3 concrete items; conclusion and CTA. Mandatory for BPO topics: lead with CTG's boundary position, never a cost-statistic opener. Title T4 or T7. Nurture.

Name the problem: every vendor claims best so the word is worthless; CTG's answer, three lenses (strategic, commercial, operational) against a documented auditable score; one concrete human-supplied mechanic; what the reader can verify themselves, as a checklist; the commercial-model line; conclusion with an offer to show the scoring. No commission rate or figure ever. Always human review. Title T3 or T1. Convert.

The pain as a question the reader is living; the uncomfortable truth a vendor will not say; what CTG has already done, with the human-supplied proof point; what the reader gets as 3-5 concrete deliverables, not benefits; the commercial model stated plainly; the ask with one low-friction action. Never the word free without the neutrality explanation. Title T8 or plain offer name. Convert. Human review on first publication.

A true concrete scene in the vertical's operational language, written as a pattern, never a named case; why the generic model breaks for this vertical's users; the 3 constraints the vertical adds (regulatory, behavioural, operational); what changes in the evaluation criteria, as a table; vertical-specific ask, no demo marathon. Never a compliance guarantee: describe requirements, never assert a solution is compliant. Always human review. Title T4 or T7.

Name and one concrete surprising fact about the Guru's practitioner history; the standing explainer of the Guru model, consultant partners assigned to clients at no cost; the specific problem this person solves, in the buyer's language; one thing they say that a vendor would not; CTA. Hard block unless consent_on_file is true; never publish a named individual off the approved roster. Always human review. Title T5. Reach.

Claim line: most [audience] pay for [thing] twice; two-beat payoff, once when X, again when Y; human-supplied proof point plus the consistent pattern in 3 concrete sentences; link CTA; hashtags last. Hook H4, reach, link_read.

Reversal claim: the thing that made you [good outcome] is the one that will [bad outcome]; negation of the expected threat; who is actually winning and why; the mechanism; what to look at first; link; hashtags. Mandatory for BPO topics, never a cost or outsourcing statistic opener. Hook H5, reach, link_read.

Repetition-loop opener: action, consequence, action again, same consequence; three parallel your-X lines naming what is stuck, empty, or burning out; one honest adjective; the actual cause in one sentence; engagement question close. Hook H6, reach, engagement CTA.

Question containing the contradiction; hint redirect that reframes it; three parallel when-your-system-fails lines; then at least 3 sentences of the article's actual argument, the post argues rather than summarises; link; hashtags. Hook H1 or H2, nurture, link_read.

Colour-scale or count question opener; the N questions that decide the answer, as a numbered list the reader can answer today; the real root cause vs the obvious culprit; comment-keyword CTA to receive the full checklist. Hook H1, nurture, comment_to_receive.

Pain question: still sitting through [category] demos that all sound the same; the part nobody selling software will say; we've already done the work, human-supplied proof point scored against the reader's workflows, seats, compliance needs; what the data says vs what the salesperson said; vendor-neutral shortlist ask with the neutrality proof; comment or DM CTA. Hook H1 or H3, convert, service_inquiry.

When every vendor says best, the word is worthless; so we don't take their word; every recommendation runs three lenses (strategic, commercial, operational) against a documented auditable score; vendor-neutral by design plus one concrete human-supplied mechanic; show-you-the-scoring ask. No commission rate, percentage, or figure ever; always human review. Hook H4, convert, service_inquiry.

Most [vertical] contact centers weren't built for today's [end users]; one human-supplied scene written as a pattern, not a named case; the fix isn't more technology, it's the right fit for how the users actually behave; sourced-comparable-settings credential; vertical ask, vendor-neutral, no demo marathon. Never a compliance guarantee; human review for regulated verticals. Hook H3, convert, service_inquiry.

Episode number with guest name, role, org; ONE concrete surprising guest practitioner fact, required and human-supplied; the claim the episode makes in one sentence; why that claim is uncomfortable or non-obvious; episode link. Hard block if no proper noun beyond the show name. Requires a paired LB-04 companion 48-72 hours later. Hook H10, reach, podcast_watch.

Guru Spotlight: name; standing Guru-model explainer, consultant partners assigned to clients at no cost for sourcing and procurement; concrete practitioner history; the specific problem they solve in the buyer's language; one thing they say a vendor wouldn't. Hard block unless consent_on_file is true; never auto-generate a person. Hook H10, reach, engagement.

N days from today, [obligation] takes effect; the exact date and statute name, human-supplied only, the agent never infers a deadline; what changes in the reader's operational terms; what breaks if unprepared; what to check first; link. Routes to regulatory human review. Never a news recap, never a third-party statistic. Hook H7, reach, link_read.

The category has a lot of [thing], very few of them worth [the reader's scarce resource]; the exception, CTG's own asset or a human-supplied item only; 2-3 concrete qualifying reasons, one line each; what the reader gets that they can't get elsewhere; single ask. The disqualified category may never be a named supplier, competitor, or third-party event: criticise the category, never a name. Hook H9, reach, engagement or link_read.

rules.name: Non-numeric proof points (numeric ones deliberately excluded)

value.text: the buyer never pays us; the supplier does
three lenses on every recommendation: strategic, commercial, operational
We didn't study contact centers. We ran them.
